# Introduction
In this presentation, I analyze the volatility of Google stock prices using GARCH models.
I implement rolling-window estimation, volatility forecasting, and stock price simulation for Jan-Feb 2025.
Finally, I evaluate model performance and select the best model for predicting Google's stock prices. These are the topics I will cover:
<br>**1. Data Loading & Preprocessing**
<br>**2. Volatility Analysis**
<br>**3. Rolling Window**
<br>**4. Price Simulation**
<br>**5. Simulated Prices vs Real Price**
<br>**6. Quantile Bands**
<br>**7. Model Validation: RMSE**

```{r Libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(quantmod)              # Load financial data (Google stock prices)
library(xts)                   # Time series manipulation
library(rugarch)               # GARCH model estimation and forecasting
library(PerformanceAnalytics)  # Financial analysis (logarithmic returns)
library(tseries)               # Statistical tests for time series (ADF test)
library(fBasics)               # Basic financial statistics (dagoTest)
library(zoo)                   # Time series manipulation and rolling window analysis
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

```

# 3. Rolling Window - Models

**sGARCH:**
$$\sigma_t^2 = \omega + \alpha_1 \epsilon_{t-1}^2 + \beta_1 \sigma_{t-1}^2$$

**gjrGARCH:**
$$\sigma_t^2 = \omega + \alpha_1 \epsilon_{t-1}^2 + \gamma_1 I_{t-1} \epsilon_{t-1}^2 + \beta_1 \sigma_{t-1}^2$$

**eGARCH:**
$$\log(\sigma_t^2) = \omega + \beta_1 \log(\sigma_{t-1}^2) + \alpha_1 \frac{|\epsilon_{t-1}|}{\sigma_{t-1}} + \gamma_1\frac{\epsilon_{t-1}}{\sigma_{t-1}}$$

```{r garch-model, echo=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
models_list <- list(
sGARCH_norm = ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)),variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH"), distribution.model = "norm"),
sGARCH_sstd = ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)), variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH"), distribution.model = "sstd"),
gjrGARCH_norm = ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)), variance.model = list(model = "gjrGARCH"), distribution.model = "norm"),
gjrGARCH_sstd = ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)), variance.model = list(model = "gjrGARCH"), distribution.model = "sstd"),
eGARCH_norm = ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)), variance.model = list(model = "eGARCH"), distribution.model = "norm"),
eGARCH_sstd = ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)),variance.model = list(model = "eGARCH"), distribution.model = "sstd"))
```

# 3. Rolling Window - Settings

```{r, echo=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
window_size <- 251  # Approx. 1 year of trading days (assuming ~252 trading days per year)
forecast_horizon <- 40  # Approx. 2 months of trading days
n_obs <- length(returns) # Total number of observations in the dataset
results <- list() # Store results for each model
```

.center[
```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=5.45, fig.width=11.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
years <- 2019:2024
trading_days_per_year <- 251
forecast_horizon <- 40
window_size <- trading_days_per_year

df <- data.frame()
for (i in 0:(length(years)-1)) {
  start <- i * window_size
  end <- start + window_size
  forecast_end <- end + forecast_horizon
  df <- rbind(df, data.frame(Start = start, End = end, Forecast = forecast_end, Year = years[i+1]))
}

df$Label <- "Rolling Window"
df_forecast <- df
df_forecast$Label <- "Forecast Period"

df_combined <- rbind(df, df_forecast)

#Plot
p <- ggplot(df_combined) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = Start, xmax = End, ymin = Year - 0.3, ymax = Year + 0.3, fill = "Rolling Window"), 
            alpha = 0.6, color = "blue") +
  
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = End, xmax = Forecast, ymin = Year - 0.3, ymax = Year + 0.3, fill = "Forecast Period"), 
            alpha = 0.6, color = "red") +

  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, 
                    values = c("Rolling Window" = "lightblue", 
                               "Forecast Period" = "lightcoral")) +
  
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, 
                     values = c("Window Shift" = "black")) +

  labs(title = "Illustration of Rolling Window Moving Over Time with Forecasts",
       x = "Trading Days", y = "Rolling Window Year") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") 

print(p)
```
]

# 3. Rolling Window - Executable Code

```{r echo=TRUE, cache=TRUE, results='hide'}
for (model_name in names(models_list)) {
  cat("Estimating rolling window for model:", model_name, "\n") 
  
  spec <- models_list[[model_name]]  
  model_results <- list() 
  forecasts <- matrix(NA, nrow = 6, ncol = forecast_horizon)  
  
  for (year in 0:5) {  
    start_index <- (year * window_size) + 1 
    end_index <- start_index + window_size - 1 
    if (end_index > n_obs) break 
    window_data <- returns[start_index:end_index]  
    fit <- ugarchfit(spec = spec, data = window_data)  
    
    if (fit@fit$convergence == 0) {  
      model_results[[year + 1]] <- fit  
      
      forecast <- ugarchforecast(fit, n.ahead = forecast_horizon) 
      forecasts[year + 1, ] <- as.numeric(sigma(forecast))  } 
      else {
      cat("Model", model_name, "for year", 2019 + year, "did not converge\n") }} 

  results[[model_name]] <- list(models = model_results, forecasts = forecasts)}  
```

# 4. Price Simulation - Settings

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.2, fig.width=11.5}
sGARCH <- ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)),
                variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH"),
                distribution.model = 'sstd')
s <- ugarchfit(data = returns, spec = sGARCH)

gjrGARCH <- ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)),
                variance.model = list(model = "gjrGARCH"),
                distribution.model = 'sstd')
gjr <- ugarchfit(data = returns, spec = gjrGARCH)

eGARCH <- ugarchspec(mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)),
                variance.model = list(model = "eGARCH"),
                distribution.model = 'sstd')
e <- ugarchfit(data = returns, spec = eGARCH)

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
plot(s, which = 12) 
plot(gjr, which = 12)
plot(e, which = 12)
```

Settings for the price simulations and Root Mean Squared Error:

```{r, cache=TRUE}
m.sim <- 100  # Number of simulations per model
n.sim <- 38   # Number of forecast days (Jan-Feb 2025)
last_price <- as.numeric(last(G$GOOG.Close))  # Last observed stock price
rmse_results <- list() # Store RMSE values for each model
model_names <- names(results) # Extract model names
simulated_prices_list <- list() # Initialize storage for simulated prices
```

```{r cache=TRUE, include=FALSE}
for (model_name in model_names) {
  cat("Simulating future prices for model:", model_name, "\n")
  last_index <- length(results[[model_name]]$models)
  
  if (last_index == 0) {
    cat("Skipping model", model_name, "due to missing estimations\n")
    next}
  last_model <- results[[model_name]]$models[[last_index]]
  if (is.null(last_model)) {
    cat("Skipping", model_name, "as the last model did not converge.\n")
    next}
  
  sfinal <- models_list[[model_name]]
  fixed_params <- as.list(coef(last_model))
  
  sfinal_fixed <- ugarchspec(
    mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0,0)),
    variance.model = list(model = last_model@model$modeldesc$vmodel),
    distribution.model = last_model@model$modeldesc$distribution)
  
  setfixed(sfinal_fixed) <- fixed_params  # Fix the parameters
  sim <- ugarchpath(spec = sfinal_fixed, m.sim = m.sim, n.sim = n.sim, rseed = 123)

  simulated_returns <- fitted(sim)
  simulated_prices <- last_price * exp(apply(simulated_returns, 2, cumsum))
  simulated_prices_list[[model_name]] <- simulated_prices}
```

# 5. Simulated Prices vs Real Price

LEGEND:
  <span style="background: linear-gradient(to right, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet);
               -webkit-background-clip: text; color:transparent">

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=6.8, fig.width=11.5, cache=TRUE}
par(mfrow = c(2,3))  # Arrange plots in a grid

# Load actual prices for Jan-Feb 2025
real_prices <- getSymbols("GOOG", from = "2025-01-01", to = "2025-02-28", auto.assign = FALSE)$GOOG.Close

# Comparing simulated prices with real stock prices.
for (model_name in model_names) {
  if (!is.null(simulated_prices_list[[model_name]])) {
    simulated_prices <- simulated_prices_list[[model_name]]
    
    plot(index(real_prices), real_prices, type = "l", col = "black", lwd = 3,
         ylim = range(simulated_prices, real_prices), main = paste(model_name),
         ylab = "PRICE", xlab = "DAYS")
    
    colors <- rainbow(m.sim)
    for (i in 1:m.sim) {
      lines(index(real_prices)[1:nrow(simulated_prices)], simulated_prices[, i], col = colors[i], lwd = 2, lty = 2)
    }
   }
}
```

# 6. Quantile Bands

LEGEND: <span style="color:black;">**Real Prices**</span>,  <span style="color:blue;">**Median Simulation**</span>,  <span style="color:gray;">**90% Confidence Interval**</span>,  <span style="color:purple;">**50% Confidence Interval**</span>

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=6.8, fig.width=11.5}
# Assume that:
# - simulated_prices_list is a list of matrices, where each matrix has:
#     rows = forecast days
#     columns = simulations (m.sim)
# - real_prices is an xts series containing the actual prices for the period of interest

par(mfrow = c(2, 3))  # Arrange plots in a grid

# For each model, I compute the quantiles for each day and plot the graphs:
for(model_name in names(simulated_prices_list)) {
  
  simulated_prices <- simulated_prices_list[[model_name]]
  
  # Compute the quantiles for each day (each row) across the simulations
  # This step uses the 'apply' function to work over the rows (MARGIN = 1) of the matrix
  # I compute the 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, and 95th percentiles
  quantiles <- t(apply(simulated_prices, 1, function(x) {
    quantile(x, probs = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
  }))
  
  # Get the forecast dates. I assume that these correspond to the first n rows of real_prices.
  forecast_dates <- index(real_prices)[1:nrow(simulated_prices)]
  
  # Set the y-axis range based on both the quantiles and the actual real prices
  y_range <- range(c(quantiles, coredata(real_prices)[1:nrow(simulated_prices)]), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Plot the real prices. The real prices are plotted as a solid black line
  plot(forecast_dates, coredata(real_prices)[1:nrow(simulated_prices)],
       type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "black",
       main = paste(model_name),
       xlab = "DATE", ylab = "PRICE", ylim = y_range)
  
  # Draw a polygon to represent the area between the 5th and 95th percentiles (this is the low-intensity zone)
  # This polygon creates a shaded band indicating where 90% of the simulations lie
  polygon(c(forecast_dates, rev(forecast_dates)),
          c(quantiles[, "5%"], rev(quantiles[, "95%"])),
          col = rgb(0.8, 0.8, 0.8, alpha = 0.5), border = NA)
  
  # Draw a polygon to represent the area between the 25th and 75th percentiles (this is the high-concentration zone)
  # This band shows the interquartile range, highlighting the central 50% of the simulations
  polygon(c(forecast_dates, rev(forecast_dates)),
          c(quantiles[, "25%"], rev(quantiles[, "75%"])),
          col = rgb(0.4, 0.4, 0.8, alpha = 0.5), border = NA)
  
  # Plot the median simulation line (50th percentile) in blue.
  lines(forecast_dates, quantiles[, "50%"], col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  
  # Re-plot the real prices line to ensure it is clearly visible on top of the polygons
  lines(forecast_dates, coredata(real_prices)[1:nrow(simulated_prices)], col = "black", lwd = 3)
}
```

# 7. Model Validation: RMSE

```{r, comment=NA}
# Evaluating model performance using Root Mean Squared Error
for (model_name in model_names) {
  if (!is.null(simulated_prices_list[[model_name]])) {
    simulated_prices <- simulated_prices_list[[model_name]]
    
    # Compute RMSE for each simulated scenario
    rmse_values <- sapply(1:m.sim, function(i) sqrt(mean((real_prices - simulated_prices[, i])^2, na.rm = TRUE)))
    rmse_mean <- mean(rmse_values)
    rmse_results[[model_name]] <- rmse_mean
    cat("RMSE for model", model_name, ":", rmse_mean, "\n")
 }
}
```

```{r echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Identifying the best model using RMSE performance
best_model <- names(which.min(rmse_results))
cat("The best model based on RMSE is: **", best_model, "** with RMSE ->**", rmse_results[[best_model]], "**\n")
```
